items.subject: package manager
items.text: The package manager is pnpm 9; do not use npm or yarn in this repo.

items.subject: node version
items.text: Node version is pinned to 20.11 in .nvmrc; run nvm use before installing.

items.subject: monorepo
items.text: The monorepo is orchestrated with Turborepo; pipelines live in turbo.json.

items.subject: env files
items.text: Never commit .env files; only .env.example is tracked.

items.subject: env setup
items.text: For local env, copy .env.example to .env.local and pull secrets from the 1Password vault acme-dev.

items.subject: commits
items.text: Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, chore:).

items.subject: pull requests
items.text: Every PR needs one approval from CODEOWNERS and green CI before merge.

items.subject: ci
items.text: CI runs on GitHub Actions; workflows are in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

items.subject: linter
items.text: Linting and formatting use Biome; run pnpm lint at the root.

items.subject: eslint
items.text: Decided to drop ESLint and Prettier in favor of Biome in March.

items.subject: module system
items.text: All packages are ESM: package.json has "type": "module".

items.subject: ERR_REQUIRE_ESM
items.text: ERR_REQUIRE_ESM fix: set "type": "module" in the package and import with the .js extension instead of require().

items.subject: path aliases
items.text: TypeScript path aliases use the @acme/* prefix, defined in tsconfig.base.json.

items.subject: exports
items.text: Prefer named exports; no default exports except Next.js pages.

items.subject: unit tests
items.text: Unit tests use Vitest across all packages.

items.subject: e2e tests
items.text: End-to-end tests use Playwright.

items.subject: coverage
items.text: Coverage threshold is 80% lines; CI fails below it.

items.subject: dependency updates
items.text: Renovate opens dependency update PRs every Monday; automerge only for patch updates.

items.subject: versioning
items.text: Versioning uses Changesets: run pnpm changeset for any user-facing change.

items.subject: answer style
items.text: User prefers concise answers with the code first and the explanation after.

items.subject: lodash
items.text: Avoid lodash; use native array methods or remeda.

items.subject: validation
items.text: Runtime validation uses zod everywhere.

items.subject: dates
items.text: Use date-fns for dates; moment is banned.

items.subject: logging
items.text: Structured logging uses pino.

items.subject: error tracking
items.text: Errors are reported to Sentry; the DSN comes from SENTRY_DSN.

items.subject: feature flags
items.text: Feature flags are managed in GrowthBook.

items.subject: analytics
items.text: Product analytics use PostHog.

items.subject: time zone
items.text: All timestamps are stored in UTC; convert to local time only in the UI.

items.subject: git hooks
items.text: Git hooks run through lefthook; husky was removed.

items.subject: python
items.text: Python scripts in tools/ use Python 3.12 managed by uv.

items.subject: sudo
items.text: Never run pnpm install with sudo; fix permissions instead.

items.subject: ports
items.text: Local ports: web 3000, api 4000, worker metrics 9464, Postgres 5432, Redis 6379.

items.subject: docker
items.text: Local containers run on OrbStack instead of Docker Desktop.

items.subject: local services
items.text: Start Postgres and Redis locally with docker compose up -d db redis.

items.subject: dev server
items.text: pnpm dev at the root starts web, api and worker together via Turborepo.

items.subject: staging
items.text: Staging is at staging.acme.dev and deploys automatically from main.

items.subject: production
items.text: Production deploys happen from git tags v*; the release workflow is release.yml.

items.subject: main branch
items.text: Never force-push to main; it is a protected branch.

items.subject: codeowners
items.text: The platform team owns infra/ and .github/ in CODEOWNERS.

items.subject: comments
items.text: User wants no comments that restate the code; comment only the why.

items.subject: editor
items.text: Recommended VS Code extensions are listed in .vscode/extensions.json.

items.subject: pnpm lockfile
items.text: Gotcha: CI uses pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, so always commit pnpm-lock.yaml after adding a dependency.

items.subject: secrets manager
items.text: Team secrets live in the 1Password vault acme-dev; production secrets are in AWS Secrets Manager.

items.subject: apple silicon
items.text: On Apple Silicon, the sharp and canvas packages need Rosetta-free builds: run pnpm rebuild sharp after switching Node versions.

items.subject: typescript
items.text: TypeScript runs in strict mode with noUncheckedIndexedAccess enabled.

items.subject: issue tracker
items.text: Issues are tracked in Linear under the ACME team; branch names start with the Linear id like acme-123.

items.subject: console.log
items.text: Do not leave console.log in committed code; use the pino logger.

items.subject: license
items.text: The repo is proprietary; the CLI package is MIT licensed.

items.subject: package manager
items.text: The package manager is yarn 1.

items.subject: node version
items.text: Node version is 18 LTS.

items.subject: web framework
items.text: The web app is Next.js 15 with the App Router.

items.subject: auth provider
items.text: The web auth provider is Clerk.

items.subject: auth provider
items.text: The web auth provider is Auth0.

items.subject: auth middleware
items.text: Clerk middleware lives in apps/web/middleware.ts and protects everything except publicRoutes.

items.subject: login page
items.text: The login page is apps/web/app/login/page.tsx and renders Clerk's SignIn component.

items.subject: redirect loop
items.text: Gotcha: the sign-in redirect loop happens when /login is missing from publicRoutes in middleware.ts; also set afterSignInUrl to /dashboard.

items.subject: styling
items.text: Styling is Tailwind CSS v4; config is CSS-first in app/globals.css.

items.subject: ui components
items.text: UI components come from shadcn/ui and live in apps/web/components/ui.

items.subject: server state
items.text: Server state uses TanStack Query; client state uses zustand.

items.subject: redux
items.text: Decided not to use Redux in the web app.

items.subject: forms
items.text: Forms use react-hook-form with zod resolvers.

items.subject: images
items.text: Remote images must be allowed in next.config.ts remotePatterns; the CDN host is cdn.acme.dev.

items.subject: public env vars
items.text: Only env vars prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_ are exposed to the browser; never put secrets in them.

items.subject: web tests
items.text: Run web unit tests with pnpm --filter web test.

items.subject: web e2e
items.text: Run web end-to-end tests with pnpm --filter web e2e; it needs the dev server on port 3000.

items.subject: storybook
items.text: Storybook runs on port 6006 with pnpm --filter web storybook.

items.subject: hydration mismatch
items.text: Hydration mismatch fix: format dates on the client inside useEffect, or use suppressHydrationWarning on the time element.

items.subject: i18n
items.text: Translations use next-intl; messages are in apps/web/messages/*.json.

items.subject: icons
items.text: Icons come from lucide-react.

items.subject: dark mode
items.text: Dark mode is handled by next-themes with the class strategy.

items.subject: api client
items.text: All browser calls to the API go through apps/web/lib/api.ts, a fetch wrapper that sends credentials: include.

items.subject: analytics provider
items.text: The PostHog provider is mounted in apps/web/app/providers.tsx.

items.subject: can't resolve fs
items.text: Build error "Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'" fix: add import "server-only" and keep the module out of client components.

items.subject: preview deploys
items.text: The web app deploys on Vercel; every PR gets a preview deployment.

items.subject: caching
items.text: Marketing pages use ISR with revalidate = 60.

items.subject: security headers
items.text: CSP and security headers are set in next.config.ts headers().

items.subject: fonts
items.text: The Inter font is loaded with next/font/google in app/layout.tsx.

items.subject: payments
items.text: Checkout uses Stripe Checkout redirect; the web app never sees card data.

items.subject: accessibility
items.text: Icon-only buttons must have an aria-label.

items.subject: bundle size
items.text: Inspect bundle size with ANALYZE=true pnpm --filter web build.

items.subject: route groups
items.text: Authenticated pages live in the app/(dashboard) route group; public pages in app/(marketing).

items.subject: server actions
items.text: Decided to use server actions for form posts instead of API routes in the web app.

items.subject: error pages
items.text: Global errors are handled in app/global-error.tsx which reports to Sentry.

items.subject: components style
items.text: User prefers small components under 150 lines and colocated tests.

items.subject: web env
items.text: The web app reads the API base URL from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL.

items.subject: clerk keys
items.text: Gotcha: Clerk dev instance keys start with pk_test_; production builds fail if pk_test_ keys are used.

items.subject: web framework
items.text: The web app is Next.js 13 with the pages router.

items.subject: api framework
items.text: The API is built with Fastify 5.

items.subject: database
items.text: The database is Postgres 16.

items.subject: orm
items.text: The ORM is Drizzle; schema is in apps/api/src/db/schema.ts.

items.subject: db migrations
items.text: Apply migrations with pnpm --filter api db:migrate.

items.subject: generate migration
items.text: Generate a new migration with pnpm --filter api drizzle-kit generate after editing schema.ts.

items.subject: api auth
items.text: The API verifies Clerk session JWTs with @clerk/backend in src/plugins/auth.ts.

items.subject: rate limit
items.text: Rate limit is 100 requests per minute per IP, stored in Redis via @fastify/rate-limit.

items.subject: api versioning
items.text: Routes are versioned under /v1.

items.subject: openapi
items.text: The OpenAPI spec is generated from zod schemas into apps/api/openapi.yaml.

items.subject: api tests
items.text: API tests run against a real Postgres started by Testcontainers.

items.subject: auth tests
items.text: Run only the auth tests with pnpm --filter api test -- auth.

items.subject: stripe webhook
items.text: Gotcha: the Stripe webhook route /v1/webhooks/stripe needs the raw body; register fastify-raw-body or signature verification fails.

items.subject: error format
items.text: Errors are returned as RFC 7807 problem+json.

items.subject: pagination
items.text: List endpoints use cursor pagination, never offset.

items.subject: soft delete
items.text: Rows are soft-deleted with a deleted_at column.

items.subject: money
items.text: Money is stored as integer cents, never floats.

items.subject: ids
items.text: Primary keys are UUID v7.

items.subject: connection pool
items.text: The Postgres pool max is 10 connections per pod.

items.subject: pgbouncer
items.text: Gotcha: PgBouncer runs in transaction mode, so prepared statements must be disabled (prepare: false).

items.subject: database url
items.text: The API reads the database connection string from DATABASE_URL.

items.subject: seed data
items.text: Seed local data with pnpm --filter api db:seed.

items.subject: email
items.text: Transactional email is sent through Resend; templates are React Email in apps/api/emails.

items.subject: jobs
items.text: The API enqueues background jobs to the worker with BullMQ.

items.subject: cors
items.text: CORS allows only origins listed in CORS_ORIGINS.

items.subject: health check
items.text: The health endpoint is GET /healthz and checks Postgres and Redis.

items.subject: request ids
items.text: Every request log carries a requestId header x-request-id.

items.subject: timeouts
items.text: Outbound HTTP calls must set a 10 second timeout.

items.subject: n+1
items.text: Gotcha: the orders list had an N+1 query; use the with: relations option in Drizzle to batch.

items.subject: file uploads
items.text: File uploads go directly to S3 with presigned URLs from POST /v1/uploads.

items.subject: search
items.text: Full-text search uses Postgres tsvector columns, not Elasticsearch.

items.subject: orm choice
items.text: Switched from Prisma to Drizzle in May because of cold-start time.

items.subject: api port
items.text: The API listens on port 4000 locally.

items.subject: migrations
items.text: Never edit a migration that has been merged; add a new one.

items.subject: multi tenancy
items.text: Every table has an org_id column and queries must filter by it.

items.subject: webhooks out
items.text: Outgoing webhooks are signed with HMAC SHA-256 in the X-Acme-Signature header.

items.subject: jwt clock skew
items.text: Gotcha: intermittent 401s came from JWT clock skew; allow 5 seconds of leeway in auth.ts.

items.subject: database
items.text: The database is MySQL 8.

items.subject: api framework
items.text: The API is built with Express 4.

items.subject: cli framework
items.text: The CLI is built with commander.

items.subject: cli bundler
items.text: The CLI is bundled with tsup into dist/index.js.

items.subject: cli package
items.text: The CLI is published to npm as @acme/cli and the binary is named acme.

items.subject: cli config
items.text: The CLI stores its config in ~/.acme/config.json.

items.subject: cli tests
items.text: CLI tests use Vitest snapshot tests of stdout.

items.subject: cli release
items.text: Release the CLI by merging the Changesets version PR; the publish job runs npm publish --provenance.

items.subject: node support
items.text: The CLI must support Node 18 and later; no newer APIs without a fallback.

items.subject: cli esm
items.text: The CLI is ESM-only; the ERR_REQUIRE_ESM error from users means they are on an old Node, tell them to upgrade to 18.

items.subject: cli auth
items.text: acme login uses the OAuth device code flow and stores the token in the OS keychain via keytar.

items.subject: cli local run
items.text: Run the CLI locally with pnpm --filter @acme/cli dev -- <args>.

items.subject: cli colors
items.text: Terminal colors use picocolors, not chalk.

items.subject: cli prompts
items.text: Interactive prompts use @clack/prompts.

items.subject: cli output
items.text: Commands must support --json output for scripting.

items.subject: cli telemetry
items.text: CLI telemetry is opt-out with ACME_TELEMETRY=0.

items.subject: windows paths
items.text: Gotcha: on Windows, config path joins broke; always use path.join and os.homedir().

items.subject: cli update check
items.text: The CLI checks for updates once a day using update-notifier.

items.subject: cli exit codes
items.text: Exit code 2 means usage error, 1 means runtime error.

items.subject: cli link
items.text: To test the CLI globally, run pnpm --filter @acme/cli build then npm link in packages/cli.

items.subject: cli framework
items.text: The CLI is built with yargs.

items.subject: queue
items.text: The worker consumes BullMQ queues on Redis 7.

items.subject: queue names
items.text: Queue names are email, images, billing-sync and webhooks.

items.subject: concurrency
items.text: Worker concurrency is 5 jobs per process.

items.subject: retries
items.text: Jobs retry 3 times with exponential backoff starting at 1 second.

items.subject: scheduled jobs
items.text: Cron jobs are BullMQ repeatable jobs defined in src/schedules.ts.

items.subject: sharp alpine
items.text: Gotcha: sharp fails on the Alpine image; the Dockerfile uses node:20-slim with libvips instead.

items.subject: dead letter
items.text: Failed jobs after the last retry move to the dead-letter queue dlq and alert in Slack #alerts.

items.subject: worker metrics
items.text: The worker exposes Prometheus metrics on port 9464 at /metrics.

items.subject: worker dev
items.text: Run the worker locally with pnpm --filter worker dev; it needs Redis running.

items.subject: job dashboard
items.text: Bull Board is mounted at /admin/queues on the worker, behind basic auth.

items.subject: idempotency
items.text: Every job handler must be idempotent; use the job id as the idempotency key.

items.subject: billing sync
items.text: billing-sync pulls Stripe invoices every 15 minutes.

items.subject: redis memory
items.text: Gotcha: Redis ran out of memory because completed jobs were kept; set removeOnComplete: 1000.

items.subject: worker shutdown
items.text: The worker drains jobs on SIGTERM with a 30 second grace period.

items.subject: image jobs
items.text: Image jobs resize uploads to 3 sizes and write WebP to S3.

items.subject: worker tests
items.text: Run worker tests with pnpm --filter worker test; they use an in-memory Redis mock (ioredis-mock).

items.subject: queue
items.text: The worker consumes RabbitMQ queues.

items.subject: iac
items.text: Infrastructure is Terraform 1.8 in infra/terraform.

items.subject: terraform state
items.text: Terraform state lives in the S3 bucket acme-tfstate with a DynamoDB lock table.

items.subject: cloud region
items.text: AWS region is us-east-1 for everything.

items.subject: kubernetes
items.text: The API and worker run on EKS; the cluster is named acme-prod.

items.subject: helm
items.text: Helm charts live in infra/helm, one chart per service.

items.subject: terraform apply
items.text: Never run terraform apply from a laptop; only the CI plan/apply workflow applies.

items.subject: terraform plan
items.text: Run make plan ENV=staging to see a Terraform plan locally.

items.subject: k8s secrets
items.text: Kubernetes secrets come from AWS Secrets Manager through External Secrets Operator.

items.subject: dns
items.text: DNS is on Cloudflare; the zone is acme.dev.

items.subject: monitoring
items.text: Metrics and logs go to Grafana Cloud; dashboards are in infra/grafana.

items.subject: alerting
items.text: Alerts page the on-call through PagerDuty.

items.subject: kube context
items.text: Switch kubectl context with aws eks update-kubeconfig --name acme-prod --region us-east-1.

items.subject: container registry
items.text: Images are pushed to ECR repositories named acme/<service>.

items.subject: database hosting
items.text: Production Postgres is RDS with Multi-AZ; backups are kept for 14 days.

items.subject: redis hosting
items.text: Production Redis is ElastiCache.

items.subject: eks upgrade
items.text: Gotcha: the EKS 1.29 upgrade broke the ingress; the AWS Load Balancer Controller must be upgraded first.

items.subject: ingress
items.text: Ingress uses the AWS Load Balancer Controller with ACM certificates.

items.subject: infra changes
items.text: Infra changes need a review from the platform team and a plan output pasted in the PR.

items.subject: autoscaling
items.text: The worker scales with KEDA on queue length; the API uses HPA on CPU at 70%.

items.subject: cost
items.text: Cost tags: every resource needs the tags team and env.

items.subject: vpn
items.text: Access to the prod database goes through Tailscale; no public endpoint.

items.subject: rds failover
items.text: RDS failover took 90 seconds in the last game day; the API retries connections for 2 minutes.

items.subject: iac
items.text: Infrastructure is Pulumi in TypeScript.

items.subject: merge policy
items.text: Never merge pull requests yourself; push to the PR branch and let the user merge.

items.subject: pr timing
items.text: Do not open a pull request until the user says the work is ready.

items.subject: branching
items.text: Always work on a feature branch; never commit directly on main.

items.subject: pushing
items.text: Do not push to the upstream remote without asking first.

items.subject: verification
items.text: Before saying a task is done, re-check the work for bugs and security issues.

items.subject: e2e before pr
items.text: Test changes end to end before opening a PR, not only unit tests.

items.subject: explanations
items.text: Explain things plainly, without jargon.

items.subject: research depth
items.text: When asked to research, go deep: read primary sources and cite them.

items.subject: deletion
items.text: Do not delete files or branches without confirmation.

items.subject: friday deploys
items.text: Never deploy to production on Fridays.

items.subject: pr size
items.text: Keep diffs small: one concern per pull request.

items.subject: new dependencies
items.text: Ask before adding a new dependency.

items.subject: generated files
items.text: Never hand-edit generated files under dist/ or *.gen.ts.

items.subject: destructive db
items.text: Do not run destructive database commands (drop, truncate, reset) without asking.

items.subject: full suite
items.text: Run the full test suite, not only the changed tests, before pushing.

items.subject: history rewrite
items.text: Do not rewrite or squash commits that are already pushed.

items.subject: summaries
items.text: End-of-task summaries should be a short bullet list.

items.subject: plan first
items.text: Show a plan before large refactors and wait for approval.

items.subject: git stash
items.text: Do not use git stash; commit work in progress to the branch instead.

items.subject: skipped tests
items.text: Never skip or disable failing tests to make CI green.

items.subject: github cli
items.text: Use the gh CLI for GitHub operations.

items.subject: billing code
items.text: Do not change billing code without the user's review.

items.subject: emojis
items.text: No emojis in code, commits or docs.

items.subject: commit body
items.text: Commit messages use the imperative mood with a short body explaining why.

items.subject: major upgrades
items.text: Do not bump major versions of dependencies without asking.

items.subject: script language
items.text: Prefer TypeScript over JavaScript for new scripts.

items.subject: secrets in logs
items.text: Keep secrets and tokens out of logs and error messages.

items.subject: uncertainty
items.text: When a fix is uncertain, say so instead of guessing.

items.subject: docs updates
items.text: Update the docs/ pages when public behavior changes.

items.subject: ci benchmarks
items.text: Do not run long benchmarks on the shared CI runners.

events.text:
Server push let the server send resources (CSS, JS) the browser hadn't asked for yet, on the same connection. In practice it often pushed things already in the browser cache, wasted bandwidth and was hard to tune, so Chrome removed it in 2022 and most CDNs dropped it. So yes, push is effectively dead.

103 Early Hints is an informational response the server sends before the real one, carrying `Link: rel=preload` or `rel=preconnect` headers. The browser decides whether to fetch, and it checks its cache first, so nothing is wasted. It mostly helps when the server needs a few hundred ms to produce the HTML: the browser uses that time to start loading fonts and CSS. Push said "here's the file"; early hints say "you'll probably want this file" and leave the browser in charge.

events.text:
Rarely. `structuredClone` handles what the JSON trick breaks: `Date` stays a `Date` (JSON turns it into a string), `Map`/`Set`, typed arrays, `undefined` values, circular references, `NaN`/`Infinity`, and `BigInt`. It's built into Node 17+ and all current browsers.

The JSON trick still makes sense in two cases: when you deliberately want a JSON-safe copy (stripping functions, class prototypes and `undefined`, e.g. before sending something over the wire), or when the object holds things `structuredClone` refuses, like functions or DOM nodes, where it throws `DataCloneError`. Neither keeps class instances' prototypes, so for those you want an explicit copy method anyway.

events.text:
`AsyncLocalStorage` (from `node:async_hooks`) gives you a value that follows one logical chain of async work. You call `als.run(store, fn)`, and anything `fn` triggers, including awaited promises, timers and callbacks, can call `als.getStore()` and get that same store, without passing it through every function argument. That's why people use it for request context: set it once in middleware, read it deep in a database helper or logger.

On speed: since Node 16 it's built on a cheaper mechanism than the old async hooks, and in current Node versions the overhead is small, typically a few percent in microbenchmarks and usually not noticeable in an I/O-bound API. The real cost is mostly clarity: hidden context is harder to follow than an explicit argument, and it breaks if some library loses the async chain (rare now, but it happens with some old callback-based code).

events.text_all: quick q while i get coffee: whats actually different between structuredClone(x) and JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))

events.text:
```js
const a = { d: new Date(), m: new Map([[1, 'x']]), u: undefined };
structuredClone(a);              // Date stays a Date, Map stays a Map, u kept
JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(a));   // d becomes a string, m becomes {}, u dropped
```

structuredClone uses the same algorithm browsers use to copy data between windows and workers. It keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays, and handles circular references. The JSON round trip only keeps plain JSON values: Dates turn into strings, Maps and Sets become empty objects, undefined and functions disappear, and a circular reference throws. Neither one copies functions or class prototypes (a class instance comes back as a plain object), and structuredClone throws on functions instead of silently dropping them.
